meta.name: V3 Engine Stability Signoff
meta.objective: Compile a compile-only workflow that defines the remaining engine-stability hardening program: per-work-unit retry semantics in engine settings, deterministic fault injection for chaos testing, final observability and forensic gaps, and the complete test/signoff matrix required before calling the engine stable.

compile.baseHint: The engine is operationally much healthier, but signoff is blocked by one remaining product-level failure mode: a single target can still fail terminally without consuming a defined retry budget. The workflow should define the smallest stability program needed to close retry semantics, deterministic chaos coverage, and final signoff criteria without reopening broad architectural work.
taskSignals: The latest sanity rerun crossed the former score-stage timeout boundary without reproducing the old failure family.

A later full loop completed operationally but the control plane marked the cohort scientifically_invalid because one score target failed with an unrecognized verdict label and its paired downstream target was blocked.
Diagnostics on the failed run show the target did not consume a three-attempt retry budget; the current behavior is effectively terminal too early for the desired policy.
Large target-level forensic queries can still exceed read limits, so observability and pagination remain part of stability signoff.
notes: This is compile-only. It defines the remaining hardening and signoff program but does not patch or relaunch anything itself.

The intended execution order is: localize retry semantics, define deterministic chaos hooks, define the signoff test matrix, adversarially challenge the plan, then synthesize one patch-and-validation roadmap.
The workflow should treat per-work-unit retry semantics as an engine-settings contract, not as ad hoc logic hidden in stage-specific code.

env: Current live cohort state from control-plane checks should be treated as context, not as a required execution input for this compile-only artifact.

stopConditions: Stop at compilation. Do not patch code, deploy runtime changes, or launch live chaos runs from this workflow artifact.
The compiled plan must produce one explicit answer for what must pass before the engine can be called stable enough for signoff.
If a proposed test or patch is not tied to a concrete observed risk, it should be pushed to backlog rather than included in the required signoff gate.
